base.rule: Preserve original bytes. This corrigendum overrides only the topics enumerated here. No prior ACK transfer.

opened_result_additions.initial_mux_cursor: Opaque integrity-protected base64url cursor,1..2048bytes, issued by trusted producer in durable OPENED result

cursor_bootstrap.cursor_binding: Exact connection_id, connection_epoch, admitted principal/session and quota owner/delegation/policy revision, initial position0, profile/schema hash and replay bounds. Contains no bearer credentials. Inner snapshot cursor never substitutes for outer mux cursor.
cursor_bootstrap.issuance: Connection allocation and immutable OPENED command receipt atomically bind initial position/cursor reference. Exact authorized duplicate OPEN returns original connection/epoch/result, not another cursor or slot. Cursor validity is separately checked; observing historical result does not revive an expired session/cursor.
cursor_bootstrap.stream_start: GET events requires initial_mux_cursor and X-Stream-Attempt-ID canonical UUIDv4. First admitted stream start durably binds attempt to connection epoch. No concurrent second delivery for the same connection. Original stream-start response loss is UNKNOWN; never retry a different attempt or attach a second socket without qualified old-delivery containment. A disconnected stream requires a fresh connection/snapshot after old slot containment, not implicit continuation.
cursor_bootstrap.first_frame: mux_sequence=1 after the admitted initial position0. Every outer frame kind, including notices and liveness, increments sequence exactly1 within that connection epoch. Overflow denies/terminates; never reset on restart.
sequence_rules: Require exact admitted connection_id/epoch before accepting any frame.
Expected next sequence applies atomically after complete outer validation.
Exact duplicate immediately last accepted sequence and identical canonical frame bytes is inert; it refreshes no authority or freshness.

Same sequence with different bytes, any sequence gap, an older non-last sequence, unknown connection epoch or unestablished starting position is a connection-level protocol failure, not a guessed per-subscription gap.
No persistent replay continuation after producer/consumer disconnect is promised. Retained command results support reconciliation only, not an authorization to resume a socket.
cursor_bootstrap.subscription_and_snapshot: SUBSCRIBED and snapshot ACK do not reissue/reset outer cursor or mux sequence. Snapshot cursor is the independently bound view-change position. Outer sequence orders interleaving across subscriptions; it does not fill an inner delta gap, verify a root or establish authority. Concurrent subscribe/snapshot-ready notices enter the same contiguous outer sequence.

canonical_command_identity.typing: UUID identities canonical lowercasev4 or explicit null where target absent; epochs canonical bounded positive u63 decimal strings or null for not-applicable. Path is canonical parsed route plus exact target IDs; no percent/empty/duplicate path aliases. Full command digest covers every field. DELETE has SHA256 of zero raw body bytes and rejects nonempty body.

headers.X-Request-ID: Canonical UUIDv4 equal to body request_id where a body exists; mandatory for DELETE
headers.Idempotency-Key: Bounded canonical ASCII ID,1..128bytes; immutable original command identity
headers.X-Expected-Connection-Epoch: Canonical positive u63 decimal string for subscription creation, snapshot ACK, connection/subscription DELETE; equal to body field if present
headers.X-Expected-Subscription-Epoch: Canonical positive u63 decimal string for snapshot ACK and subscription DELETE; equal to body field if present
headers.X-Stream-Attempt-ID: Canonical UUIDv4 for first events GET; stream-start identity distinct from admission request_id
headers.X-CSRF-Token: Provider-validated human-cookie CSRF token; separate from idempotency and never a quota credential

canonical_command_identity.cross_target_reuse: Idempotency ledger scope is quota owner+original actor principal+key. Reusing same key for different method/operation/path/target/epoch/body/session/request conflicts even if DELETE bodies are both empty. Do not include target in the lookup key in a way that makes cross-target reuse silently new.
canonical_command_identity.unknown_vs_rejection: Transport loss/unverified commit is UNKNOWN, never role/epoch rejection. A definitive role/epoch rejection requires current verified provider/authority decision and original command receipt reconciliation. HTTP409 alone does not prove a lost earlier command failed.
canonical_command_identity.authorized_reconciliation: GET /control/v3/commands/<request_uuid> returns current-authorized original immutable admission receipt/outcome. Current HUMAN owner or explicitly admitted delegated service may read only its permitted original command scope. New authenticated session may read historical result under a real ReconcileControlAdmission capability, but cannot impersonate original session, alter command digest, replay original cursor as current, mint another slot or rekey unresolved command. Missing/unavailable receipt remains UNKNOWN until qualified reconciliation establishes resolution.
canonical_command_identity.reauthenticated_recovery: Historical OPENED receipt/cursor bound to an old session is evidence only. Current-authorized close/drain may target that old connection using a NEW explicit command and expected epoch, never an altered retry of the old command. New connection requires qualified old-slot release or an actually free reserved slot. No automatic session alias or silent reattachment.

connection_failure: Incomplete or assembly-deadline-exceeded outer SSE event
Oversize outer frame or noncanonical/unparseable JSON
Invalid outer schema/hash/connection/epoch or unknown mux sequence gap
Conflicting duplicate or unauthenticated outer frame
Unvalidated subscription identity or inconsistent null connection-notice target
failure_attribution.connection_action: Immediately clear LIVE for ALL subscriptions on that connection, discard every incomplete/partially applied frame, stop accepting that delivery epoch and close/drain connection. Global slot is not reusable until independently qualified termination/containment. Error notice is best effort under byte caps, never required for local failure detection. Other independently admitted connections retain their own state/freshness.
failure_attribution.subscription_failure: Only after complete authenticated outer validation establishes exact current subscription_id/epoch may an inner domain/root/change-sequence/snapshot/payload error be isolated to that subscription. Clear its LIVE and resnapshot; other subscriptions may continue on intact contiguous outer transport. No partial inner change apply.
failure_attribution.clarification: Review2 'clear only affected subscription' applies ONLY to attributable inner failures. It does not apply to outer framing/transport identity/sequence failures.

required_negative_vectors: OPENED issues position0 and first outer frame1; snapshot cursor cannot bootstrap mux
Lost OPEN/stream-start response reconciles original identity without new socket/slot
Last exact duplicate inert; conflicting duplicate/gap/old epoch clears all connection subscriptions LIVE
Same empty DELETE key on different target/method/epoch conflicts
Reauthenticated historical read does not revive original cursor/session or permit rekey
Incomplete/oversize/unparseable outer frame clears all; authenticated attributable inner error isolates one
Concurrent subscribe/snapshot ACK never resets outer sequence
remaining_full_abi_dependencies: Pinned closed request/result/error/frame/payload schemas and exact hashes by agreed schema editor
Qualified real human/service delegation, CSRF, global command/slot/epoch/byte/encoder registry
Independent old-delivery containment, actual two-producer8physical9logical load/relocation evidence
Source/domain caps, actual authority read barriers and measured native/socket/memory/time limits
